title: ci(test-shards): place Test Core bins by predicted wall, and cut the CLI into 4 slices on the refreshed dataset
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DGuXpcS2tMB1v58Jdn3L7NW)_

Part of #25870. This PR carries two steps: (1) wall-based bin placement, and (2) the refreshed dataset with the CLI cut into 4 slices. #25870 stays open, because its acceptance is measured on 3 consecutive spec-touching PRs after landing. The prediction below is not that measurement.

**Supersedes #25960.** It carries the shard-timings-refresh lane's commit 92343f5b (`chore(ci): refresh the Test Core shard-timings dataset`) unchanged. That refresh cannot land alone, because pin 3c refuses it at 3 slices (step 2).

## Diagnosis — which of the three, with run ids

The long shards are always the three that carry a `@objectstack/cli` file-level slice. Read from `gh api …/runs/N/jobs` step timings on 56 `pull_request` runs (2026-10-25 18:54Z – 2026-10-26 05:44Z), and from the slice leg's own `Duration` / turbo `Time:` lines on the 18 slice-shard jobs of six `packages/spec`-touching runs.

The slowest shard on a spec-touching PR breaks down like this (minutes):

| run (spec PR) | slowest | setup | closure | whole-package leg | cli slice leg (turbo `Time:`) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 40274911131 (#25903) | 5/8 28.8 | ~1.5 | 6.0 | 5.7 | 15.4 |
| 40271593540 (#25944) | 4/8 28.1 | ~1.5 | 5.5 | 3.4 | 17.3 |
| 40269339195 (#25813) | 4/8 28.5 | ~1.5 | 5.6 | 3.4 | 17.5 |
| 40266487909 (#25903) | 5/8 28.5 | ~1.5 | 5.9 | 5.6 | 15.4 |
| 40263851511 (#25813) | 3/8 26.8 | ~1.5 | 6.3 | 4.5 | 14.3 |
| 40261969569 (#25830) | 3/8 25.7 | ~1.5 | 6.0 | 4.3 | 13.6 |

(whole-package leg = `Run this shard's tests` minus the slice leg's turbo `Time:`.)

Three causes, all real, in this order of size:

1. **The cli slice leg itself, 13.6–17.5 min.** vitest cuts the CLI by file COUNT (`BaseSequencer.shard`: sha1 of the path, then equal-count chunks), so the three slices are not equal: across the six runs they measured 518–1047 s, the heaviest ~1.27× the mean (~820 s). Total cli 2406–2542 s against a pinned 2899 s (0.83–0.88×).
2. **The dependency closure, 5.5–6.3 min**, against 0.4–1.0 min on shards that skip declarations. `@objectstack/cli` is in ci.yml's `DTS_READERS`, so every slice shard builds the whole cli closure WITH `.d.ts`, and a PR run reads no remote cache, so that build is cold (ci.yml: local cold closure 5m59s with declarations, 1m24s without).
3. **A whole-package leg of 2.2–5.7 min run before the slice — the partitioner's doing.** `partition()` balanced bins by their SUM of predicted seconds. A slice runs serially after the four-wide whole leg, so the step is ~ wholeSum / 2.9 + slice (the #25376 wall model). Balancing sums filled every slice shard up to the mean with ~900 s of whole packages: predicted step 1277 s on the three slice shards against 643 s on the other five (committed dataset, full list).

Stale weights are not the cause: on the refreshed dataset (#25960, the shard-timings-refresh lane's 2026-10-26 output) the sum-placed split still predicts 1107 s on the slice shards against 518 s elsewhere — the same 2.1× gap.

## Step 1: wall-based placement (cause 3)

In `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`, with no workflow or package edit:

- `partition()` places bins by **load** — the wall model in whole-package seconds, a slice counting `WHOLE_LEG_PARALLELISM` (2.9, the #25376 constant, reused rather than re-derived) times its weight. A list with no slice is placed by exactly the same additions and comparisons as before, so every non-sliced run (and the nightly, which slices every package on every shard) gets a byte-identical split.
- `total` stays the plain sum, so the density cap and the drift report mean what they meant. `refineToCap()` keeps `load` in step with `total`.
- `balanceOf()` also reports the walls; pin 2 grades the wall ratio (with a slice in the split the sums are unequal by design); new pin 2b is a fixture where sum-placement and wall-placement differ.
- The shard log prints the predicted walls under the bins line.

Predicted test steps, full list (`turbo ls`, dogfood excluded), via `planRun()`:

| dataset | before (slice shards / others) | after (slice shards / others) |
|---|---|---|
| committed (2026-10-23) | 1277 s / 643 s | 966 s / 830 s |
| #25960 refresh (2026-10-26) | 1107 s / 518 s | 899 s / 642 s |

Measured-based expectation for the six spec runs above: removing the whole-package leg takes the slowest shard from 25.7–28.8 min to **~22.3–25.1 min**. The other five shards absorb the moved packages (their slowest was 17.5 min; +~2.5 min of four-wide work each).

## Step 2: the refreshed dataset, and the CLI at 4 slices

The refresh (92343f5b, 14 runs, newest 40272142430) measures `@objectstack/cli` at 2697.45s. Pin 3c (`sliceCountProblems`, the serial-floor derivation of #22075) then refuses 3 slices:

| n | one slice | vs the heaviest other serial task (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 670.12s; spec and runtime run as two tasks) | limit 1.3x = 871.16s |
|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 3 | 899.15s | 1.34x | refused: "Raise it to 4" (this is #25960's red, job 121437007857) |
| 4 | 674.36s | 1.01x | meets, and 3 does not, so 4 is the smallest |

So the change is `FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` cli 3 → 4, with `PREVIOUS_FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` set to the outgoing `{cli: 3}` per the map's own rule, so the refresh lane still decodes the 3-slice summaries retained from before the change. The docblocks carry the new derivation table. The bin-sum floor and the wall model agree on this dataset, and no ratio or bound moved. Predicted test-step walls on the full list are 738s on all 8 shards (max/mean 1.00x), and every bin is within the density cap.

**Predicted from measurement, not from the model.** vitest's `BaseSequencer.shard` (sha1 of the path relative to the package root, sorted, equal-count chunks) reproduced locally over `vitest list --filesOnly` (506 files) matches run 40274911131's three slice jobs file for file: 169/169/168 files on jobs 121415631670/…679/…708. From those jobs' per-file times, with the wall taken as 0.39 × the per-file sum (vitest's `Duration` over its `tests` sum on the same jobs: 0.403/0.381/0.390):

| split | predicted slice walls | measured (vitest `Duration`) | heaviest / mean |
|---|---|---|--:|
| 3 ways | 789 / 691 / 926 s | 812.65 / 673.01 / 921.52 s | 1.15 |
| 4 ways | 487 / 616 / 673 / 630 s | — | 1.12 |

The heaviest slice falls 27%. Applied to the six spec runs (slowest = setup ~1.5 + that run's cold DTS closure + ~1.1 min of whole leg, the wall model's 738 − 674 s, + 0.727 × that run's heaviest slice):

| run (spec PR) | slowest before | predicted after both steps |
|---|--:|--:|
| 40274911131 (#25903) | 28.8 | 19.8 |
| 40271593540 (#25944) | 28.1 | 20.7 |
| 40269339195 (#25813) | 28.5 | 20.9 |
| 40266487909 (#25903) | 28.5 | 19.7 |
| 40263851511 (#25813) | 26.8 | 19.3 |
| 40261969569 (#25830) | 25.7 | 18.5 |

That gives 18.5–20.9 min, with three of six at or under 20. The cost: a fourth shard now builds the CLI's DTS closure (~5.8 min cold). The 738s walls above count test time only, not that build. The per-file read of 5/8 lacks 11 files that print before the 5,000-line log tail; their 172.2s (vitest `tests` minus the captured sum) is spread evenly over them.

## If the readings stay above ~20 min

What is left on a slice shard is the cold DTS closure (5.5–6.3 min) plus the heaviest slice. The next steps, neither taken here:

- **B. Declarations only where a slice reads them.** Three CLI test files read built `.d.ts`. With the split now reproducible, a slice holding none of them could build DTS-off (~1 min instead of ~5.8). This edits `ci.yml`, so it is Tier H.
- **C. Weight-balanced CLI slices** (a sequencer splitting by measured file time): heaviest/mean 1.12 → ~1.0. It needs a per-file weight source that the dataset does not carry today.

## Acceptance notes

- **Deliberate leftovers in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Tier H, untouched):** the Test Core header still says each slice is "placed at its PLAIN weight so every bin keeps the whole-package split's density", and its "3 slices" wording (the drift-step comment, "a shard carrying one of its 3 slices is predicted a third of that"; the timeout history) is now stale. Correcting either makes a PR Tier H, so both are left for whichever step edits ci.yml. The partitioner's own headers carry the corrected statements.
- Slice shards now come out as shards 1–4 on the full list (LPT places the heaviest loads first). Shard numbers carry no meaning beyond the per-shard Turbo seed key.

## Tests

- `node scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs --self-test` at b3234103 → `self-test OK (75 measured packages -> 78 shard items, 8 shards, predicted test-step walls 738/738/738/738/738/738/738/739s, max/mean 1.00x <= 1.3x, …, file-level slices: @objectstack/cli x4)`.
- Step 1 revert proof (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, bin choice back to `total`, on the committed dataset): the self-test reds with `balance: at 8 shards the slowest predicted test step is 1.45x the mean (1277s vs 881s)`. Restored blob == HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Step 2 revert proof: the refreshed dataset with cli at 3 reds pin 3c with `@objectstack/cli: sliced 3 ways at 2697.45s, one slice is 899s -- past 1.3x the heaviest other serial task (670s, so 871s) … Raise it to 4.` (the same red as #25960's job 121437007857).
- `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` is byte-identical to 92343f5b (`git diff 92343f5b b3234103 -- scripts/test-shard-timings.json` is empty).
- Sibling self-tests are green at b3234103: `measure-test-shard-timings` (decodes through both maps), `check-test-completeness`, `ci/select-shard-timings-run`, `nightly-tiers`, `check-test-suite-ceilings`, `ci/select-shard-packages.selftest.sh`.

## Gates

- Local derived set at b3234103 (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, merge-base origin/main cdd4eea9): all 35 families exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads `35 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 35 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`. Step 1 alone (8ca31e08) ran its 33 families the same way.
- Everything else (Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core, …) belongs to CI and is read from this PR's check-runs.
